decisions.reason: The candidate already has a complete same-message MODIFY recording mastery of the new variation, shorter-format, and hook-selection approach as an advancement prerequisite; no additional change is required.
Counting hook variations as separate clip versions does not change the requirement that clips receive client approval before counting or publication.
The variation-counting rule does not determine clip duration; the separate shorter-style clause is already represented by same-message duration events.
Allowing multiple hook variations from one body clip does not alter the submission channel, folder format, deadline, or review-link workflow.
The qualification process was already completed, and the new production counting rule does not modify that historical qualification state.
Reusing a body clip with different hooks does not change the permitted source materials or the existing video-selection constraint.
The source changes how clip versions may contribute toward production but does not change which clips are authorized for publication or where they are published.
Changing a hook while reusing the body does not relax or modify the requirement that each clip deliver a complete standalone lesson, story, or point.
The variation-counting rule does not alter the clean editing, effects, or transition standards.
Permitting a changed hook to create another version does not modify caption color, font, effects, lettering, or position.
The source permits hook variations and announces hook training but does not change the candidate's trial-local standard for selecting impactful source moments.
The clip-variation counting decision has no effect on the requirement to remove distracting wind noise.
